claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a dual-phase FCC+B2 microstructure and is ductile.
At approximately 600°C, the FCC matrix reaches a critical L12 ordering state approaching a stoichiometric Ni3Al-like composition.
Chemical ordering in FCC high- or medium-entropy alloys can affect their mechanical properties.
The non-monotonic evolution of L12 order in the FCC matrix modulates antiphase-boundary energy.
The non-monotonic evolution of L12 order modulates stacking-fault energy.
A high degree of L12 order increases antiphase-boundary energy.
High antiphase-boundary energy raises the barrier to screw-dislocation cross-slip.
Aging near 600°C produces jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
The combination of inhibited cross-slip and jagged B2/FCC interfaces forces deformation into planar slip bands.
Planar slip bands generate dislocation pile-ups and stress concentrations at interface serrations that can exceed interface cohesive strength and cause brittle fracture.
At approximately 750°C, thermal energy exceeds the ordering enthalpy and reduces L12 long-range order.
Reduced L12 order at 750°C lowers antiphase-boundary energy.
Lower antiphase-boundary energy restores cross-slip, suppresses planar-slip localization, and restores ductility.
Aging at 750°C relaxes the interface morphology or produces compliant ductile transition zones along phase boundaries.
Tensile elongation has a minimum near 600°C.
L12 domain size and order parameter peak in the 600°C-aged condition.
The 600°C-aged material exhibits planar slip bands terminating at jagged B2/FCC interfaces and a high density of pinned dislocations.
The 750°C-aged material exhibits reduced order, frequent cross-slip, wavy slip traces, and smoother or more compliant interface zones.
The brittle transition occurs above an L12 order parameter of approximately 0.6, when antiphase-boundary energy makes the cross-slip barrier critical.

If simple phase decomposition rather than ordering controls embrittlement, slip should remain wavy and cross-slip-active while mobility is reduced by precipitate shearing, and interface roughness should not correlate with slip planarity.
